Subject: Legal read — Sapphire exclusivity / MFN language

Team —

I reviewed the clause language in the SOW and Sapphire's commercial_summary. Key legal risks and recommendations below: 

- MFN / benchmark clause risks: The language is vague ("comparable customers" and "market benchmarks"). That creates an indefinite obligation to monitor and potentially match future customer-specific discounts or custom terms. Exposure compounds over time and across products.
- Exclusivity risk: A 12-month exclusivity tied to a vertical + geography can impede go-to-market with other customers and hamper partnerships with channel/integrator partners.

Recommendations (legal edits):
1) Replace MFN with a narrow "price-protection" clause: 
   - Limit to named comparable customers (we propose a list of up to 3 named accounts that Sapphire can propose at signing) and apply only within 90 days after contract execution.
   - Any adjustment is a one-time credit limited to unused committed credits; no perpetual repricing.
2) Exclusivity: Approve only time-boxed pilot exclusivity: 
   - Limit to <= 90 days and to the exact integration in the SOW and to the named geography. Add a carveout for existing partner channels and open-source model usage.
3) Discount governance: Approve up to 20% pilot discount. >20% requires executive (Head of Sales) approval and Deal Desk concurrence.

If sales wants to proceed with 12 months or a broader MFN, we will need an explicit business case signed by VP Sales and COO with quantifiable marketing/co-investment and legal indemnities. I’ve attached redlines for the SOW (Sapphire_Redlines_v1.docx).

Rishi
VP, Legal & Compliance
